## Chapter 1

The pale Usher—threadbare in coat, heart, body, and brain; I see him now—ever dusting his old lexicons and grammars with a queer handkerchief mockingly emblazoned with all the flags of all nations; he loved to dust his old grammars; it somehow mildly reminded him of his mortality.
“While you take in hand to school others … leaving out … the letter H … you deliver that which is not true.” —Hackluyt.
“WHALE … Sw. and Dan. hval … from roundness or rolling.” —Webster.
“WHALE … from the Dut. and Ger. Wallen; A.S. walw-ian, to roll, to wallow.” —Richardson.
Hebrew: חו. Greek: κητος. Latin: CETUS. Anglo-Saxon: WHŒL. English: WHALE. French: BALEINE. Spanish: BALLENA.

## Chapter 2

It will be seen that this mere painstaking burrower and grub-worm of a poor devil of a Sub-Sub has gone through Vaticans and street-stalls, picking up higgledy-piggledy whale allusions; take them not for gospel cetology, but for a glancing bird’s-eye view of what has been said, thought, fancied, and sung of Leviathan by many nations and generations.
So fare thee well, poor devil of a Sub-Sub. Thou belongest to that hopeless, sallow tribe no wine will ever warm; yet one sometimes loves to sit with thee, and grow convivial upon tears. Give it up, Sub-Subs! The more pains ye take to please the world, the more thankless ye go. Gulp down your tears and hie aloft to the royal-mast—there, ye shall strike unsplinterable glasses!

## Chapter 3

“And God created great whales.” —Genesis.
“Leviathan maketh a path to shine after him; one would think the deep to be hoary.” —Job.
“Now the Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah.” —Jonah.
“There go the ships; there is that Leviathan whom thou hast made to play therein.” —Psalms.
“In that day … the Lord … shall punish Leviathan the piercing serpent … and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.” —Isaiah.

“And what thing soever besides cometh within the chaos of this monster’s mouth … down it goes … and perisheth in the bottomless gulf of his paunch.” —Holland’s Plutarch’s Morals.
“The Indian Sea breedeth the most and the biggest fishes … the Whales and Whirlpooles called Balaene.” —Holland’s Pliny.
“… a great many Whales and other monsters … one … of a most monstrous size … open-mouthed … beating the sea before him into a foam.” —Tooke’s Lucian, The True History.
“He … catched … some … forty-eight, some fifty yards long.” —Other’s narrative taken down by King Alfred, A.D. 890.

“… the sea-gudgeon retires into [the whale’s mouth] in great security, and there sleeps.” —Montaigne, Apology for Raimond Sebond.
“Let us fly, let us fly! Old Nick take me if it is not Leviathan….” —Rabelais.
“This whale’s liver was two cartloads.” —Stowe’s Annals.
“The great Leviathan that maketh the seas to seethe like boiling pan.” —Lord Bacon’s Version of the Psalms.
“Touching that monstrous bulk … an incredible quantity of oil will be extracted out of one whale.” —Bacon, History of Life and Death.

“The sovereignest thing on earth is parmacetti for an inward bruise.” —King Henry.
“Very like a whale.” —Hamlet.
“… Like as the wounded whale to shore flies thro’ the maine.” —The Faerie Queene.
“Immense as whales … trouble the ocean till it boil.” —Davenant, Preface to Gondibert.
“Nescio quid sit.” —Sir T. Browne, Of Sperma Ceti.

“… ponderous tail … grove of pikes appears.” —Waller, Battle of the Summer Islands.
“By art is created that great Leviathan, called a Commonwealth….” —Hobbes, Leviathan.
“Silly Mansoul swallowed it … as if it had been a sprat in the mouth of a whale.” —Pilgrim’s Progress.
“That sea beast Leviathan … Created hugest that swim the ocean stream.” —Paradise Lost.
“… Hugest of living creatures … spouts out a sea.” —Paradise Lost.

“The mighty whales … have a sea of oil swimming in them.” —Fuller.
“So close behind some promontory lie the huge Leviathan … and swallow in the fry.” —Dryden, Annus Mirabilis.
“They cut off his head … tow it with a boat … aground in twelve or thirteen feet water.” —Thomas Edge, Voyages to Spitzbergen.
“… whales sporting … fuzzing up the water through their pipes and vents….” —Sir T. Herbert’s Voyages.
“… huge troops of whales … proceed with … caution….” —Schouten’s Sixth Circumnavigation.

“The Jonas-in-the-Whale … the first discoverer has a ducat….” —A Voyage to Greenland, 1671.
“… a whale … of the whale-bone kind … besides a vast quantity of oil … 500 weight of baleen. The jaws … stand for a gate….” —Sibbald’s Fife and Kinross.
“… Sperma-ceti whale … fierce and swift.” —Richard Strafford’s Letter from the Bermudas, 1668.
“Whales in the sea God’s voice obey.” —New England Primer.
“… more [whales] in those southern seas … by a hundred to one….” —Captain Cowley, 1729.

“… the breath of the whale … insupportable smell … disorder of the brain.” —Ulloa’s South America.
“… petticoat … armed with ribs of whale.” —The Rape of the Lock.
“… the largest animal in creation.” —Goldsmith, Natural History.
“If you should write a fable for little fishes, you would make them speak like great whales.” —Goldsmith to Johnson.
“… a dead whale … towing ashore.” —Cook’s Voyages.

“They stand in so great dread … afraid to mention even their names … carry dung, lime-stone, juniper-wood … to terrify….” —Uno von Troil, Letters on Iceland, 1772.
“The Spermacetti Whale … an active, fierce animal….” —Jefferson’s Whale Memorial, 1778.
“What in the world is equal to it?” —Burke on the Nantucket Whale-Fishery.
“The right to royal fish, which are whale and sturgeon … the property of the king.” —Blackstone.

“Rodmond … the barbed steel….” —Falconer’s Shipwreck.
“… the ocean serves on high, up-spouted by a whale in air….” —Cowper.
“Ten or fifteen gallons of blood are thrown out of the heart at a stroke….” —John Hunter.
“The aorta of a whale is larger … than the main pipe … London Bridge….” —Paley’s Theology.
“The whale is a mammiferous animal without hind feet.” —Cuvier.
“In 40 degrees south … the sea being then covered with them.” —Colnett.

“… from dread Leviathan to insect millions….” —Montgomery, World before the Flood.
“Io! Paean! … Not a mightier whale than this….” —Charles Lamb, Triumph of the Whale.
“… a green pasture where our children’s grand-children will go for bread.” —Obed Macy, History of Nantucket.
“… a gateway … by setting up a whale’s jaw bones.” —Hawthorne, Twice-Told Tales.
“… a monument … for her first love, who had been killed by a whale….” —Hawthorne.

“‘Tis a Right Whale … he threw up a pair of as pretty rainbows….” —Cooper’s Pilot.
“… whales had been introduced on the stage….” —Eckermann with Goethe.
“My God! Mr. Chace … we have been stove by a whale.” —Owen Chace, Narrative of the Essex.

“… the phospher gleamed in the wake of the whale….” —Elizabeth Oakes Smith.
“… line … nearly six English miles…. Sometimes the whale shakes its tremendous tail … cracking like a whip….” —Scoresby.
“… matter of great astonishment … the Sperm Whale … neglected….” —Thomas Beale, 1839.
“The Cachalot … better armed … and … the most dangerous to attack….” —F. D. Bennett, 1840.

“There she blows … thar she blows—bowes—bo-o-os!” —J. Ross Browne, Etchings of a Whaling Cruise, 1846.
“The Whale-ship Globe … horrid transactions….” —Lay and Hussey, Globe Mutiny.
“… preserved by leaping into the water….” —Tyerman and Bennett, Missionary Journal.
“Nantucket … adding largely every year … by the boldest industry.” —Daniel Webster.
“The whale fell directly over him, and probably killed him in a moment.” —Cheever, The Whale and his Captors.
“If you make the least damn bit of noise … I will send you to hell.” —Life of Samuel Comstock.

“… laid-open the haunts of the whale.” —McCulloch’s Commercial Dictionary.
“… haunts of the whale … clews to that same mystic North-West Passage.” —Something unpublished.
“… impossible to meet a whale-ship … without being struck by her air….” —Currents and Whaling, U.S. Ex. Ex.
“… large curved bones … arches over gateways … ribs of whales.” —Tales of a Whale Voyager.
“… ship in bloody possession of the savages….” —Taking and Retaking of the Hobomack.
“… few ever return in the ships … they departed.” —Cruise in a Whale Boat.
“… a mighty mass emerged … shot up perpendicularly … it was the whale.” —Miriam Coffin.
“… manage a powerful unbroken colt … rope tied to the root of his tail.” —Ribs and Trucks.
“… two … slowly swimming … within less than a stone’s throw of the shore.” —Darwin, Voyage of a Naturalist.
“‘Stern all! … for your lives!’” —Wharton the Whale Killer.
“So be cheery, my lads … while the bold harpooneer is striking the whale!” —Nantucket Song.
“Oh, the rare old Whale … King of the boundless sea.” —Whale Song.
